data.long_meaning: One who is devoted and submissive to Allah Almighty. The name Ablah signifies a person who is committed to following the path of truth and righteousness as ordained by Allah. The name Ablah carries the meaning “Servant of Allah” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ablah usually hope their child will grow to embody servant of allah and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ablah is believed to have originated from the Arabic language, where it means “submissive, devoted, and obedient to Allah." In Islamic culture, the name is held in high esteem, as it represents a noble character trait. It is often given to children as a reminder of their religious duties and obligations towards Allah and their community. The name Ablah is a source of inspiration, symbolizing piety and devotion.
data.spiritual_significance: For followers of Islam, the name Ablah carries great spiritual significance. It is a constant reminder of the need to be submissive and obedient to Allah, and to strive towards leading a virtuous and righteous life. The name instills a sense of humility and servitude, as well as a deep connection with the divine. As a result, the bearer of this name is encouraged to be a good example for others and to strive towards eternal happiness in the hereafter.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah, Volume 8, page 238. The name Ablah carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The Battle of Hunayn took place in 632 CE, and one of the captives was a woman named Ablah bint Hisham. She was the sister of Khalid ibn Al-Walid, the great Sword of Allah (saw) in early Islamic military history. Ablah was known for her beauty and was taken as a gift for the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) by Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, one of his commanders. The Prophet (pbuh) subsequently gave her to Umm Salamah, one of his wives, to be her companion and servant.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Tabari's Tarikh al-Rusul wa al-Muluk, Volume 2, page 427. The name Ablah carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ablah bint Abi Sufyan was a renowned poetess of the pre-Islamic era in Mecca. She was a member of the powerful clan of Umayyad, and her poetry was known for its depth and beauty. She was especially known for her qasidahs, a form of Arabic poetry. Her works were memorized and recited by various tribes in the Arabian Peninsula, and her influence extended beyond her own people.
